headline: DO: get the Comanche counter onto paper — she has had your $295K + $7K since 10:30 and every step of this deal so far has lived in text messages · WATCH: 2368 Ridge Trail's contract FELL THROUGH and it is genuinely back on market at $559K, while 16896 Whispering Pines closes today with nobody having cleared it since 7/23.

notes: ✅ CLIENT DAY IS EXECUTING, NOT JUST PLANNING. Fifteen routine runs since midnight and zero BLOCKED lines. Between 8:14 and 8:18 this morning FIVE client reports went out with live Zillow view-and-save counts on each — five sellers who were described as 'silent' or 'undebriefed' on the 7:50 board have now heard from you today, two have already replied warmly, and the Monday Review Preview shipped a 2.0 template with one-tap share links along the way. Your One Thing closed itself before noon: your seller ruled the counter at 9:32, you delivered it at 10:30, and the 5:41 AM promise to the other side was kept ninety minutes early.

🔁 THE BIGGEST CORRECTION OF THE DAY IS A GOOD ONE — 2368 RIDGE TRAIL IS BACK ON MARKET. For ten days every board said the MLS was 'wrong' because it read ACTIVE on a house that was sold. It was not wrong. The contract fell through, and you confirmed it yourself at 7:38 this morning when you wrote to two co-op agents that it is available again at $559,000. That flips the whole story: the tours the machine was counting as burned are four live prospects with no line behind them, two of the agents have already been re-approached, and the one whose buyer objected to the EIFS still thinks the house is gone.

⚠️ THREE ROUTINE HICCUPS, ALL RESOLVED OR CONTAINED. Chrome was unreachable for the 7:20 Review Preview — you reconnected it mid-run and the live crawl completed at 8:20, and Buffer analytics came back with it after a 17-day block. Inbox triage lost its Zapier Gmail actions and finished on the native connector instead. And at 11:01 the instant responder HELD a seller lead rather than touching it: the API says it is yours, the person record still carries the Lead Pond, and the rule when those two disagree is to stop. That hold is the system working.

callBlock.why: 🔴 THIS FILE CLOSES TODAY AND NOBODY HAS SAID IT IS CLEAR. It is now afternoon on the day of, and the last substantive word on this closing was 7/23 — the lender saying the file had been in for final since that morning, had not been picked up, could not close Monday, and that the borrower had slow-walked documents. Since then every sweep, including all three today, has returned nothing from either the lender or the closing coordinator. Nothing is known to have been DENIED; the honest state is that nobody has affirmatively cleared it in four days. It is an institutional seller, so there is no client waiting on your voice and no relationship at risk — which is exactly why it keeps getting skipped. One phone call resolves four days of silence in either direction, and if it is not closing today you want to know that this afternoon, not tomorrow morning

callBlock.who: Cassie C. — the paperwork, not the price
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE NUMBER IS DONE. WHAT IS NOT DONE IS ANYTHING IN WRITING. Your seller ruled it at 9:32 — counter at $295K with $7K, washer and dryer stay — and you delivered it to her at 10:30 with the appliance clarification attached. The gap between the two sides is now half what it was this morning. Two things are still open and neither is about price. First, their pre-approval letter is papered at $280,000 — below their own previous counter, let alone the number now in front of them. Nobody has asked for an updated one, and that, not the spread, is the real risk on this deal. Second, every step of this negotiation from the original offer forward has lived in text messages. The moment she says yes, it needs to be a signed counter, not a thumbs-up. Ask for the letter now rather than after acceptance, so the lender's re-paper happens in parallel instead of adding days at the back

🔴 A LISTING AGREEMENT IS EXPIRING AND THE DATE EXISTS NOWHERE IN YOUR EMAIL. Second expiry notice landed at 10:41 this morning and the full body was read: the brokerage's template never states a date — it only says to log into the portal. Five days of this system implying that date was sitting unread in an inbox, and it is not there and never will be. Pull it in the portal, or simply ask him what he signed. ✅ And correct one thing the morning board had wrong: he has NOT heard nothing. Your portfolio report went to him at 8:18 with real numbers on all three of his properties. The under-contract file shows a close date of 8/14, and the inspection that had an HVAC contractor at that house ran 10:30 to 11:30 — it is behind you now, so the useful question on this call is what the contractor actually found, not whether anyone is worried. The condo has 341 views and 22 saves at 87 days; the third property still has two public prices

🔥 REBOOK THE CANCELLED SHOWING — THE REST OF THIS FILE MOVED WITHOUT YOU THIS MORNING. Sunday's 3:00 showing cancelled at 11:44 because the buyer got called into work; that is a reschedule, not a lost buyer, and the co-op agent's number is on the notice. It is the one open item here, because the other two closed themselves: your seller got a full weekly report at 8:17 with 883 Zillow views and 45 saves on it, so the eight-day silence is over, and the agent who toured 7/23 finally answered at 8:22 — not interested, with a concern about the foundation and the concrete, which you forwarded to your seller two minutes later. That is a real objection worth pricing into the conversation. ⭐ And the lever is still live: the buyers behind the conditional re-offer are listing their own house TODAY. Until theirs is under contract that offer has no legs — the day it goes live is the day to ask for movement

🔥 STILL THE LOUDEST UNANSWERED LEAD ON THE BOARD, AND NOW THE OTHER SIDE IS CHASING YOU ON HIS BEHALF. The listing agent on one of the four houses he named himself asked directly whether his buyers had decided — she is asking because her seller is asking. He has raised his hand three separate times: a text, a voicemail, and now this. He is selling in Georgia and buying with 1031 money, which means a federal identification clock is the reason he keeps surfacing, and it is why quiet days cost more on this file than anywhere else. One call gets you in-or-out on that house plus the other three, then trip dates, then the second tour booked before you hang up. The six-listing brief drafted for him on 7/8 has still never gone out — send it while you are on the phone. This has now waited through a full weekend on top of nine days

callBlock.who: Mark N. — day three of a warm reply
callBlock.why: 🔥 A DECISION-MOMENT REPLY IS GOING COLD AND EMAIL IS THE WRONG CHANNEL. "That is a huge difference and gives us a lot to think about" came in Saturday morning, and he put BOTH his office and his cell number in the signature — that is an invitation, not a sign-off. ⚠️ DO NOT TEXT: his SMS is not landing. And do not answer it with another email — there is a stack of unsent drafts to him already, several written before the luxury tour this conversation is even about, and one of them is 36 days old. This is the two-and-a-half-million-dollar tour buyer. A reply like that dies quietly if the only thing that follows it is more typing

callBlock.who: Gail S. — referral, four days old
callBlock.why: SHE OFFERED YOU A REFERRAL BY NAME AND ASKED FOR A CALLBACK. Voicemail Friday afternoon about someone in Springville — which happens to be where you held an open house on Sunday and where you just sent a seller report showing 715 views and 38 saves. So you have something real and current to say when you call. A referral offer is the cheapest listing at-bat on this entire board, and this morning's forecast says the year now needs roughly three appointments a week from here. This is exactly what Client Day is for, and it has waited through a weekend

A SELLER RAISED HER HAND ON HER OWN HOME AND IS NOW FOUR DAYS OLD. Chelsea address, came in Friday, ownership verified as yours. Seller hand-raises are the highest-value inbound shape you get — one of these becoming a listing does more for the 45 than a week of buyer calls, and the corrected forecast says the gap has to be closed with listings taken inside the next thirteen weeks, not spread across the rest of the year. Two more of the same shape are sitting behind her from the weekend, and three fresh home-value leads landed today

You delivered it at 10:30 with the appliance clarification and the note that additional interest makes further movement unlikely. And everything from the original offer forward has lived in text messages; the moment she accepts, it needs a signed counter, not a thumbs-up. ⚠️ Still unanswered since 7/16: whether the earlier ARC Realty offer is alive. If it is, your seller is choosing between two offers rather than waiting on one

listings.status: 🔥 BACK ON MARKET — the contract fell through, $559K, four live prospects

For ten days every board carried it as 'Clear to Close Wednesday, MLS still wrongly reads ACTIVE' and counted the week's buyer tours as burned. The MLS was not wrong. The contract fell through and the house is genuinely available again at $559,000 — confirmed by your own words at 7:38 this morning to two of those co-op agents: 'It had been spoken for, that contract has fallen through, and it is back on the market.' ⭐ THAT MEANS THOSE TOURS ARE NOT WASTE, THEY ARE YOUR WARMEST PROSPECT LIST — four agents walked real buyers through in eight days, three of them inside 26 hours, every one believing the house was already sold. ⚠️ One counting correction this board owes you: the Saturday 3:00 and 3:45 records are the SAME appointment rescheduled — they share a confirmation number — so it is four tours, not five. Two agents were re-approached this morning by email; do not send them a second one. The third, whose buyer said 'too high' but named the EIFS as the reason, gets a CALL — and that same call can finally offer her the Lake Crest backup position nobody has ever offered her. ⚠️ THE PRICE CASE IS MIXED, NOT SETTLED: the 7/19 read said the price was 'JUST RIGHT' and lost on schools and yard size. Find out what actually killed the contract — an appraisal answer is data, one opinion is not. ⚠️ Quote $559,000 only; $545,000 was the dead contract's estimated close

listings.note: 🟡 THE 10:30 IS BEHIND YOU. The second inspection — the one whose showing remark read verbatim 'Meeting hvac company' — ran 10:30 to 11:30 this morning, and the useful question now is what the contractor actually found rather than whether anyone should be worried. ✅ Your seller was NOT left in the dark: a portfolio report went to him at 8:18 AM carrying this file at $899,000, under contract, closing 8/14. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED, and it still matters: that anything is wrong with the HVAC, what a contractor found, what it would cost, or that any of it threatens the close. The buyer side opened Saturday with 'I know we are on a time limit,' the buyers are described as very concerned, and nothing has gone to them in writing; a date, even an imperfect one, converts worry into a timeline. ⚠️ The proposed and ratified close dates still disagree and nobody has reconciled them. listings.note: 🟡 THE CONTRACT SAYS TOMORROW AND THE LENDER SAYS NEXT WEEK, AND TODAY IS THE LAST DAY THAT GAP CAN BE PAPERED CLEANLY. The sign showed up yesterday' — which ANSWERS the open wrong-sign item, so stop chasing it. She replied at 10:52: 'Love this information!' Get an answer today so she is not chasing you for it tomorrow. She is the kind of client who asks once, politely, and then wonders

pipeline.note: 🔴 THE CORRECTED NUMBERS FROM THIS MORNING STAND, AND THEY ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS BOARD. Verified at 7:15 today: 20 personal closings and a pace of 35 — BEHIND the 45 goal by about ten, not ahead of it. This board carried 27 and a pace of 49 as recently as last night. The cause was one unchecked caveat: a mid-June note claimed the CRM could not separate your closings from the team's, so every routine stopped checking and reported account-wide totals as yours. The export's agent column is in fact fully populated — zero blanks in 1,379 rows. That single assumption told you that you were ahead of goal for six weeks while you were behind it. ✅ THE CORRECTION ALSO CARRIES BETTER NEWS THAN THE HEADLINE: your average sale price is about $534K, not the $425K the model assumed, and average GCI per closing is about $13.2K, not $10.5K. You are selling fewer, larger houses than anyone thought — the quality of the book is stronger than the count. ⚠️ ONE NUMBER IS STILL GENUINELY UNKNOWN: the 50% net assumption is contradicted by five actual payout receipts showing 79–98%, mean 92%. That unresolved question swings the year by roughly $194K, so never state a take-home figure without saying which assumption it rests on. Ten minutes settles it. THE MATH THAT MATTERS NOW: at 60–75 days contract-to-close, anything closing in 2026 has to be under contract by about October 31 — thirteen weeks, not the rest of the year. Most of the remainder has to come from deals not yet started: roughly 1.6 contracts and 3 appointments a week. That is why the referral voicemail and the seller hand-raises on today's call block matter more than they look. ⚠️ AND ONE DATED-BOARD CHANGE TODAY: 2368 Ridge Trail's contract fell through, so it comes OFF the risk-weighted closing list and goes back onto the active-inventory list. Remaining dated board: Whispering Pines TODAY still uncleared, 683 Flag TOMORROW on paper with the lender saying Aug 3–4, 2704 19th St N Friday, then Lake Crest 8/14. Team annualizes ~58 against 90; the team's own pulse this morning reads 31 listings taken of 54.
